from, beside, to
from, beside, to (preposition)

a preposition constructed with three cases, genitive, dative and accusative. F. H. Rau wrote a dissertation on the use of the preposition παρά, published at Leipzig in 1870 and reprinted in G. Curtius' Grammatical Studies, third volume.
παρά with the genitive
παρά is most common after verbs (especially after verbs of receiving, hearing, coming)
παρά with the genitive in anastrophe πάρα
παρά with the dative: at, near, beside, with local meaning not rarely transferred to things in which one is engaged.
παρά with the accusative: to, beside, of motion to a place, just as with the genitive it signifies motion from a place.
παρ᾽ οὐδέν: of no account, not at all.
παρά with the accusative: beyond, contrary to.

The grammarians distinguished παρά with the genitive from ἀπό, which has the same meaning, in that ἀπό signifies motion from inanimate things, παρά from animate things: see Ammon. p. 20, schol. Hom. Il. 12, 114, Eustath. p. 895, 35 1134, 37, a rule true in itself but not consistently observed, as examples from Homer and others collected in the Thesaurus vol. 6 p. 192 show.
